_DESIGN_RULE: Every archetype exists to teach exactly ONE play pattern, and its numbers and actions are chosen to force that pattern rather than to decorate it. State the pattern in 'pattern' before writing any numbers; if you cannot state it in one sentence, the archetype is not designed yet. A RESOURCE archetype moves one number off base so you can always tell which resource you are failing at; a READ archetype leaves the numbers alone and differs only in priors. Priors must be reliable but not certain - 'top' interests are seeded into ranks 1-3 and 'bottom' into 7-9, everything else shuffles, and prior_slip means each seeding can fail - because a prior that is never wrong is a lookup table, not a read. Actions are TELEGRAPHED on arrival: you play around known behaviour, and stepping in the trap is on you. Keep at least two archetypes in the player's favour, or the system reads as punishment instead of personality - a favour can be an action (Tech pays a premium) or a property (Family First never gets harder, Lay-Down starts low).

archetypes.name: Easygoing
archetypes.pattern: This is how the loop works.
archetypes.tell: pleasant, unhurried, no strong opinions about anything

archetypes.name: Lay-Down Larry
archetypes.pattern: Take the free money and LEAVE - they are worth two fast sales, not six ticks of optimising.
archetypes.tell: already nodding, and has not asked a single question

archetypes.name: Budget Hawk
archetypes.pattern: Over-build appeal BEFORE you ask, and pay for it in margin.
archetypes.tell: brought a printout, and keeps saying 'out the door'

actions.name: Tells you what the other guy quoted
actions.tell: ANY offer that falls short moves their line +5
actions.line: "I had another dealer at less than that."

archetypes.name: Tire Kicker
archetypes.pattern: Do not diagnose. Sell them SOMETHING, now.
archetypes.tell: keeps glancing at the lot, half out of the chair already

actions.name: Half out of the chair already
actions.tell: every 4 ticks they are on the floor, they lose 2 more patience
actions.line: "How long is this going to take?"

archetypes.name: Tech Enthusiast
archetypes.pattern: Hunt the bullseye. Do not grind a mediocre product upward when the right one pays a premium.
archetypes.tell: asked about the drivetrain before asking about the price

actions.name: Pays up for the right toy
actions.tell: a sale on their 1st or 2nd interest banks an extra $300

archetypes.name: Family First
archetypes.pattern: Sell them their favourites, fast. They never get harder - but fishing below their top five bleeds them.
archetypes.tell: there are two car seats in the trade-in

actions.name: Not what they came in for
actions.tell: offering anything outside their top five costs 4 patience, sold or not
actions.line: "...that's really not what we're here for."

archetypes.name: The Karen
archetypes.pattern: See to them FIRST, and give them what they actually came in for.
archetypes.tell: has already asked who the manager is, twice

actions.name: Asks for the manager, loudly
actions.tell: every 5 ticks, EVERYONE ELSE on the floor loses 1 patience
actions.line: "Is there someone else I can speak to?"
